name: timer
title: Timer
description: Named countdown timers and pomodoros: the soonest one counts down on the bar and turns into an alarm when it ends. Built on the `timer` command line tool, so timers started in a terminal show up here too.
author: pal

settings.label: timer command
settings.description: The timer CLI (a name on PATH or a path). It keeps the timers; pal only reads and asks.

settings.label: State directory
settings.description: Where the CLI keeps one file per timer (its TIMER_DIR). ~ is expanded.

settings.label: Pomodoro break
settings.description: Minutes of break after a round.

settings.label: Pomodoro long break
settings.description: Minutes of break after the last round of a cycle.

settings.label: Pomodoro rounds
settings.description: Work rounds per cycle before the long break.

duration.description: 25m, 90s, 1h30m, 2:30, or minutes as a bare number

name.description: Optional; the duration otherwise. A name already taken restarts that timer

ring.description: Ring the phone out loud when it lands

timers.title: Timers
timers.description: Every timer with what is left; New timer takes a duration, a name and whether to ring the phone in the bar; Start Pomodoro runs work and break timers in turn.

keys.title: Add the minutes typed in the bar (five when blank)
Skip to the pomodoro's next phase

timer.title: Timer
timer.description: The soonest timer's remaining time with a fill; an alarm once it lands; hidden with none running. The popover: the soonest timer's time left as its headline, a card with a bar for each other one, pause, add five minutes, stop, a field to start one, a pomodoro's phase and round on its card.

ending.title: Nearly landed, another timer behind it

keys.title: Pause, resume or dismiss the timer with the ring
Move the ring to another timer (or click a card)
Start one: type 25m tea in the field, Enter
Skip to the pomodoro's next phase

store.tagline: Named countdowns and pomodoros, with an alarm on the bar
features: One row per timer, most urgent first, with the time left or when it ended
Start one by typing `25m`, `90s` or `1h30m` and a name; optionally ring the phone when it ends
`enter` pauses, resumes or dismisses; `cmd++` adds minutes (five when none are typed); `cmd+d` stops
Pomodoro: 25 minutes of work, 5 of break, 15 after the fourth round; `cmd+s` skips a phase
A bar item with the countdown filling blue to amber to red; its popover pauses, adds time or starts a timer
The same timers as the `timer` CLI, so one started in a terminal is in this list

screenshots.caption: Every timer, the most urgent first: one that just landed, three running with when each lands, one paused, and the pomodoros done today
A running timer's actions: pause it, stop it, or add the minutes in the field beside the search (five unless you type more)
A pomodoro round is a timer too: its row says the round and the phase, and skips to the break or stops the cycle
New timer, typed after the search: a duration as you would say it, an optional name, and whether the phone rings when it lands
On the menu bar: what is left of the soonest timer, with a fill under the glyph that turns amber past two thirds
A timer that landed: the item turns into a red alarm with its name
A click opens the popover: a card per timer with the time left and a bar; space pauses, + adds five minutes, backspace stops
A landed timer sits on top, red and full, until space dismisses it
n opens the field: 25m tea starts one, and the last durations are a click away
A pomodoro on the popover: the round and the phase on its card, s skips to the break, the rounds finished today below
On sketchybar: the fill as a rule of box-drawing cells before the glyph, the countdown as the label

actions.title: Pause / Resume / Dismiss
actions.description: Pause a running timer, resume a paused one, dismiss a landed one.

actions.title: Add minutes
actions.description: The minutes typed in the bar, five when blank.

actions.title: Start
actions.description: On New timer: the bar takes the duration (required), a name and Silent or Ring the phone, then the CLI starts it.

actions.title: Start pomodoro
actions.description: The Start Pomodoro row: the first work round's timer, the breaks and the next rounds follow on their own.

actions.title: Skip to the next phase
actions.description: On the pomodoro's timer: this phase's timer stopped, the next started.

actions.title: Stop pomodoro
actions.description: The cycle is over; the timer stopped.
